Not for redistribution without written consent of Morgan Stanley Morgan Stanley RESEARCH Idea July 31, 2026 04:36 AM GMT Amazon.com Inc | North America AWS's Rule of 70 and ROIC Deliver AWS delivered accelerating growth, surging profitability and a better backlog to give the market even more confidence in ROIC ahead. Retail was generally in-line but signal on grocery, robotics and agentic are all building. Raise EPS '27/'28 EPS by 2%/3%, PT to $335 (30% upside), OW. AWS’s Rule of 70 Showcases GenAI ROIC: AWS's ~840bp growth acceleration to 36.8% y/y growth (vs us at 34%) speaks to its pole position in the age of GenAI adoption in training and inference. AWS AI ARR grew 67%, or $10bn Q/Q, reaching $25bn (15% of total AWS ARR), while Non-AI Revenue accelerated to ~low-20s% Y/ Y growth, from ~19-20% Y/Y growth in 1Q. This speaks to AWS's ability to attach non-AI services (like Graviton, see here) to AI loads...and the still strong demand for its core tools. AWS's $496bn backlog (up $132bn q/q) was 5%, or ~$20bn better than expected. This, in our view, continues to be an important indicator of durable multi-year growth to come at AWS. While higher margin net accounting with Bedrock plays a role, AWS profitability was indeed impressive as incremental margins rose to ~52% (excluding a 1x item)...the highest incrementals since 4Q:24. We believe this was driven by capacity optimizations, Bedrock, accelerating core, etc. Note, as we detailed in Internet: The Paths to 25-50% GenAI ROIC (27 Jul 2026), we see the incremental margins of the hyperscalers through this GenAI age of inference approaching 30%-70%+...with AWS results speaking to the profitability ahead. Let us know if interested in our GenAI ROIC models.

However, AWS added the most EBIT dollars sequentially at $2.5bn vs Google Cloud at $2.2bn. Note, we do not believe this is an apples to apples comparison: GOOGL's TPU sales flow through as gross revenue increasing its revenue added, whereas AWS recognizes revenue sharing for 3P model consumption through Bedrock on a net basis. Ex-TPU sales, we estimate Google Cloud added $3-4bn revenue q/q, lower than AWS and closer to Azure's ~ $3.9bn Q/Q. On the other hand, TPU sales have a structurally lower margin, and AWS adding more EBIT dollars on a smaller revenue add sequentially speaks to strength of profitability as AI demand ramps.

Excluding this 2Q26 AWS margins/incremental margins would have been 38%/52%. Raising '27/'28 Capex to $325bn/$350bn: AWS's strong and accelerating ROIC justifies more spend and we expect this to continue as we raise our forward capex. We appreciated the color from AMZN management about the longer-lived (buildings, etc.) vs shorter lived (network/chips/servers) items that impact capex, as we continue to use this in our capex bottom up estimation. Please let us know if interested in our bottom up cost per GW or capex build files. Retail Investments Driving Growth and Profitability Too: Retail revenue results/ guidance were generally in-line as was profitability. Note, Retail EBIT benefitted from a 1x ~$600mn tariff-related refund tailwind, but we believe this was offset by a ~$1.1bn headwind from transitory macro fuel and line-haul costs. Excluding this net ~$500mn headwind, we estimate Retail EBIT would have been $11.3bn (7.2% margin), generally in-line with our $11.6bn (7.4% margin). Fulfillment cost per unit efficiency was notably strong, coming in 2% below us, and 17% y/y unit growth was the fastest since 1Q21 (we acknowledge the Prime Day tailwind). We see a long runway for further efficiency improvements in fulfillment + shipping costs, in particular with robotics as detailed here. Indeed, AMZN continues retrofitting facilities with the latest generation technology and expects to more than double its fleet of robotic arms, like Cardinal and Sparrow in 2026. It's encouraging AMZN's Retail investments are bearing fruit as well, specifically in faster delivery, grocery/ perishables, and agentic. The number of monthly active perishables customers grew over 50% since the start of the year, same-day orders with perishables average over Morgan Stanley Research

Morgan Stanley RESEARCH 3x more units per order, and fresh groceries now make up 6 of the top 20 best sellers on Amazon.com. Agentic adoption is growing, as over 350 million customers have now used Alexa for Shopping in the last 12 months, and engagement accelerated in Q2 with active users nearly doubling and interactions up over 5x year over year. As detailed in Internet: Agentic Shoppers Are Coming… Who Could Win or Lose? (17 Nov 2025), we continue to see AMZN as one of the companies best positioned to drive agentic commerce. Raise '27 EPS by 2%, PT to $335 (~30% Upside): We raise our AWS '27 revenue by 2% to 41% y/y growth (vs. 40% prior). Please let us know if interested in our bottom up AWS model (includes revenue/watt, AI vs non AI revenue, and backlog). We model AWS margins of 40% in '27, as AWS generates $101bn of EBIT and makes up ~60% of company-wide EBIT. This higher AWS EBIT offsets lower '27 Retail EBIT as we adjust for lower than expected N.America Retail and Merch Margins. In all, our new $335 PT implies paying ~25X '27/'28 EPS and still implies an 50% discount to its peers on a PEG basis. We remain OW.
